title: N5 foundations
description: Build the essential kana, words, kanji, and grammar that make beginner Japanese readable.

categories.title: Hiragana
categories.description: The rounded script for native Japanese words and grammar endings.

modules.title: The five vowel sounds
modules.summary: Meet あいうえお and the rhythm beneath every Japanese word.

content.intro: Japanese begins with five steady vowel sounds. Learn the symbol and sound together before relying on romaji.

sections.heading: The foundation row
sections.body: Read left to right: あ is a, い is i, う is u, え is e, and お is o.

example.japanese: あ い う え お

sections.heading: Practice aloud
sections.body: Point to each kana, say it once, then read the whole row smoothly. Japanese vowels stay short and clear.

questions.prompt: Which kana makes the sound u?
Which sequence is in standard vowel order?
Match each kana to its sound.

modules.title: The K-row
modules.summary: Read かきくけこ and combine a consonant with each vowel.

content.intro: The K-row uses a clean k sound before each vowel. The vowel order stays the same.

sections.heading: A repeated pattern
sections.body: か is ka, き is ki, く is ku, け is ke, and こ is ko.

example.japanese: か き く け こ

sections.heading: Read in pairs
sections.body: Say the vowel row, then the K-row. Notice how the final sound changes while the order stays fixed.

modules.title: The S- and T-rows
modules.summary: Add さしすせそ and たちつてと to your reading toolkit.

content.intro: Most S- and T-row sounds follow the vowel pattern, with two special readings to notice: し is shi and ち is chi.

sections.heading: Two useful rows
sections.body: Read さしすせそ as sa, shi, su, se, so and たちつてと as ta, chi, tsu, te, to.

example.japanese: さしすせそ · たちつてと
example.reading: sa shi su se so · ta chi tsu te to

sections.heading: Notice the exceptions
sections.body: Treat し, ち, and つ as whole sounds rather than forcing them into a simple spelling rule.

modules.title: The N-, H-, and M-rows
modules.summary: Read three more regular rows and begin spotting kana in words.

content.intro: The N-, H-, and M-rows extend the same vowel order. They appear often in beginner vocabulary.

sections.heading: Three patterns
sections.body: なにぬねの, はひふへほ, and まみむめも follow the a-i-u-e-o rhythm.

example.japanese: なにぬねの · はひふへほ · まみむめも
example.reading: na ni nu ne no · ha hi fu he ho · ma mi mu me mo

sections.heading: A sound to remember
sections.body: ふ is usually written fu in romaji, though its sound is softer than a strong English f.

modules.title: The Y-, R-, and W-rows
modules.summary: Complete the main hiragana table and read common short words.

content.intro: The Y-, R-, and W-rows complete the basic gojūon table. The R-row uses a light tap between r and l.

sections.heading: The final rows
sections.body: やゆよ and らりるれろ are regular patterns. The basic W-row includes わ and を.

example.japanese: や ゆ よ · ら り る れ ろ · わ を
example.reading: ya yu yo · ra ri ru re ro · wa o

sections.heading: A grammar kana
sections.body: を is normally pronounced o when it marks an object, even though its spelling is wo.

questions.prompt: How is を usually pronounced as a particle?

modules.title: Dakuten and small kana
modules.summary: Read voiced sounds, contracted sounds, and the small っ pause.

content.intro: Small marks change kana sounds. A dakuten creates voiced sounds, while small やゆよ combine with kana to make one syllable.

sections.heading: Marks and combinations
sections.body: か becomes が with dakuten. きゃ combines ki and small ya into kya. Small っ doubles the next consonant.

example.japanese: がっこう · きょう

sections.heading: Read the shape
sections.body: Look for the small character and the two short strokes. They carry sound information, not decoration.

questions.prompt: Which kana has a voiced g sound?
Complete the word for school: が___こう
What does small っ usually do?

categories.title: Katakana
categories.description: The angular script used for loanwords, names, emphasis, and foreign terms.

modules.title: Katakana vowels and K-row
modules.summary: Meet アイウエオ and カキクケコ.

content.intro: Katakana represents the same sounds as hiragana with sharper, more angular shapes.

sections.heading: Same sounds, new shapes
sections.body: Learn ア イ ウ エ オ and カ キ ク ケ コ as a second visual set.

example.japanese: ア イ ウ エ オ

sections.heading: Use the context
sections.body: Katakana often signals a loanword, a foreign name, or emphasis.

modules.title: Katakana S-, T-, and N-rows
modules.summary: Read サシスセソ, タチツテト, and ナニヌネノ.

content.intro: The middle katakana rows mirror hiragana sounds, including the special shi, chi, and tsu readings.

sections.heading: Three rows
sections.body: Read サシスセソ, タチツテト, and ナニヌネノ in vowel order.

example.japanese: サラダ · テスト

sections.heading: Loanword practice
sections.body: These rows appear in familiar borrowed words, so read the whole word rather than isolated symbols only.

modules.title: Katakana H-, M-, Y-, R-, and W-rows
modules.summary: Complete the most useful katakana rows.

content.intro: These rows appear in names, food, technology, and everyday borrowed vocabulary.

sections.heading: Read by vowel
sections.body: ハヒフヘホ, マミムメモ, ヤユヨ, ラリルレロ, and ワヲ follow familiar patterns.

example.japanese: ホテル · ミルク

sections.heading: Keep a visual notebook
sections.body: Write confusing pairs beside their hiragana partners and read them in short words.

modules.title: Dakuten and small katakana
modules.summary: Read voiced sounds and contracted combinations in loanwords.

content.intro: Katakana uses dakuten, handakuten, and small vowels to represent sounds in foreign words.

sections.heading: Expanded sounds
sections.body: ガ, ザ, ダ, バ, and パ are voiced or plosive versions of familiar rows. Small ャ, ュ, ョ create combinations.

example.japanese: シャツ · ティー

sections.heading: Listen for the detail
sections.body: A small vowel can change the rhythm and sound of a word, especially in imported vocabulary.

questions.prompt: What does small ャ do in シャ?

modules.title: Loanwords and long vowels
modules.summary: Read familiar borrowed words using ー and small vowel patterns.

content.intro: A long vowel is marked with ー in katakana. Many everyday modern words are written this way.

sections.heading: Stretch the vowel
sections.body: コーヒー has long o and long i sounds. Read the long mark as an extra beat.

example.japanese: コーヒー · スーパー

sections.heading: Read from sound
sections.body: Break a loanword into beats first, then connect the sounds into a natural word.

questions.prompt: What does コーヒー mean?
Which mark lengthens the vowel in スーパー?

categories.title: Kanji
categories.description: Recognize a practical first set of characters through meaning, shape, and context.

modules.title: Numbers and counters
modules.summary: Recognize the first number kanji and use them in simple phrases.

content.intro: Number kanji are among the most useful characters because they appear in prices, dates, ages, and times.

sections.heading: Start with one to three
sections.body: 一 is one, 二 is two, 三 is three, and 四 is four. Learn the meaning before every possible reading.

example.japanese: 一 二 三 四 五

sections.heading: Context chooses the reading
sections.body: Numbers change pronunciation with counters, but recognition comes first at this level.

modules.title: Days, dates, and time
modules.summary: Read the kanji that organize calendars and daily schedules.

content.intro: 日, 月, 火, 水, 木, 金, and 土 appear in weekdays, calendars, and time expressions.

sections.heading: Nature in the calendar
sections.body: The weekday kanji connect to sun, moon, fire, water, tree, gold, and earth.

example.japanese: 月曜日 · 日曜日

sections.heading: Read the ending
sections.body: 曜日 means weekday. Learn it as a useful visual ending after learning the day character.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means day or sun?
What does 水 suggest in weekday names?
Which kanji means month or moon?

modules.title: People and family
modules.summary: Recognize 人, 女, 男, 子, and family-related characters.

content.intro: People kanji help you recognize names, labels, and beginner sentences about family.

sections.heading: A small people set
sections.body: 人 means person, 女 woman, 男 man, 子 child, and 友 friend.

example.japanese: 友だち · 男の子

sections.heading: Build meaning in context
sections.body: A kanji gives a visual clue even when you do not know every reading yet.

modules.title: Nature and common places
modules.summary: Recognize 山, 川, 田, 口, and 駅 in simple signs and words.

content.intro: Place and nature kanji often appear on maps, station signs, and names.

sections.heading: Visual landmarks
sections.body: 山 is mountain, 川 river, 田 rice field, 口 mouth or opening, and 駅 station.

example.japanese: 山 · 川 · 駅

sections.heading: Look for compounds
sections.body: Characters become more useful when you notice them inside a longer word or location name.

modules.title: Core verbs and descriptions
modules.summary: Meet a practical set of action and quality kanji.

content.intro: A few high-frequency kanji make short sentences easier to recognize.

sections.heading: Action characters
sections.body: 見 is see, 行 go, 来 come, 食 eat, and 大 big. These appear constantly in beginner material.

example.japanese: 大きい · 食べる

sections.heading: Learn the word
sections.body: Kanji readings vary, so learn each character inside a useful word rather than as an isolated flashcard only.

questions.prompt: Which kanji means eat in 食べる?
What does 行 mean in 行く?

categories.title: Vocabulary
categories.description: Useful first words for everyday situations and simple conversations.

modules.title: Greetings and introductions
modules.summary: Open a conversation and say who you are.

content.intro: A few polite phrases let you greet people, thank them, and introduce yourself.

sections.heading: Reliable openings
sections.body: こんにちは is hello, ありがとう is thank you, and はじめまして is nice to meet you.

example.japanese: はじめまして。

sections.heading: Close with confidence
sections.body: Say よろしくおねがいします after an introduction when you want to express goodwill.

questions.prompt: What does こんにちは mean?
Which phrase means nice to meet you?
Which phrase is used before sleep?

modules.title: Numbers and classroom language
modules.summary: Count, ask questions, and name common study objects.

content.intro: Numbers and classroom words are useful from the first day of study.

sections.heading: Useful objects
sections.body: ほん is book, えんぴつ is pencil, and つくえ is desk.

example.japanese: これは ほんです。

sections.heading: Ask for repetition
sections.body: わかりません means I do not understand. もういちどお願いします asks politely for one more time.

questions.prompt: Which means I do not understand?
What does もういちど mean?

modules.title: Family and people
modules.summary: Talk simply about yourself, friends, and family.

content.intro: Family words often change slightly depending on whether you speak about your own family or someone else's.

sections.heading: Start with familiar words
sections.body: ともだち is friend, かぞく is family, and きょうだい is siblings.

example.japanese: わたしの かぞく

sections.heading: Keep it simple
sections.body: Use の to connect a person to a group: わたしのともだち means my friend.

questions.prompt: What does ともだち mean?
What does わたしの mean?

modules.title: Food and shopping
modules.summary: Recognize basic food, prices, and shopping phrases.

content.intro: Food words and simple requests make a first visit to a shop or café less intimidating.

sections.heading: Everyday food
sections.body: みず is water, ごはん is rice or a meal, and りんご is apple.

example.japanese: みずを ください。

sections.heading: Ask politely
sections.body: ください means please give me. いくらですか asks how much something costs.

questions.prompt: Which phrase means how much is it?
What does ください do in みずをください?

modules.title: Places and directions
modules.summary: Name common places and ask where something is.

content.intro: Place words pair naturally with どこ, the question word for where.

sections.heading: Find your way
sections.body: えき is station, がっこう is school, and みせ is shop.

example.japanese: えきは どこですか。

sections.heading: Simple direction words
sections.body: みぎ is right, ひだり is left, and まっすぐ is straight ahead.

modules.title: Daily activities and adjectives
modules.summary: Describe a normal day with high-frequency words.

content.intro: A small group of verbs and adjectives helps you describe what you do and what things are like.

sections.heading: A daily rhythm
sections.body: おきます is get up, ねます is sleep, and はたらきます is work.

example.japanese: まいにち はたらきます。

sections.heading: Describe simply
sections.body: おおきい is big, ちいさい is small, and おもしろい is interesting.

questions.prompt: What does おもしろい mean?

categories.title: Grammar basics
categories.description: Make clear beginner sentences with particles, nouns, verbs, and adjectives.

modules.title: Sentence order and です
modules.summary: Introduce a topic and make a polite statement.

content.intro: A useful beginner frame is X は Y です. The topic comes first and です closes a polite statement.

sections.heading: A dependable frame
sections.body: わたしは がくせいです means I am a student. は is written ha but read wa here.

example.japanese: わたしは がくせいです。

sections.heading: Make it yours
sections.body: Replace the topic or description while keeping the sentence frame stable.

questions.prompt: Which means I am a student?
options: わたしは がくせいです。
がくせいは わたしです。
わたしが おはようです。
questions.answer: わたしは がくせいです。

questions.prompt: Complete: わたし ___ がくせいです。
Which word closes the polite statement?

modules.title: は, も, and の
modules.summary: Mark topics, add also, and connect nouns.

content.intro: Particles show how words relate. は marks a topic, も means also, and の connects one noun to another.

sections.heading: Three small connectors
sections.body: わたしは I, わたしも I also, and わたしの my show three useful relationships.

example.japanese: これは わたしの ほんです。
example.reading: Kore wa watashi no hon desu.

sections.heading: Swap one piece
sections.body: Keep the structure and change only the person or object to create new sentences.

questions.prompt: Complete: わたし ___ がくせいです。
In わたしのほん, what does の connect?
What does わたしも mean?

modules.title: これ・それ・あれ
modules.summary: Point to things near you, near someone else, or far from both.

content.intro: Japanese uses a three-way pointing system. これ is near me, それ near you, and あれ far from both.

sections.heading: Point clearly
sections.body: この, その, and あの come before a noun: このほん means this book.

example.japanese: これは なんですか。

sections.heading: Ask and answer
sections.body: Use なんですか to ask what something is, then answer with a simple noun sentence.

questions.prompt: Which word means this thing near me?
Which is correct for this book?

modules.title: あります and います
modules.summary: Say that objects and living things exist or are located somewhere.

content.intro: あります is used for objects and plants. います is used for people and animals.

sections.heading: Two existence verbs
sections.body: ほんがあります means there is a book. ねこがいます means there is a cat.

example.japanese: へやに ねこが います。
example.meaning: There is a cat in the room.

sections.heading: Location first
sections.body: に marks the place where something exists. Ask どこにありますか or どこにいますか.

questions.prompt: Which verb is for a person?
Which sentence says there is a cat?
What does に mark here: へやにいます?

modules.title: を, に, and で
modules.summary: Mark objects, destinations, times, and places of action.

content.intro: Particles become practical when you describe an action. を marks what you act on, に marks a destination or time, and で marks where an action happens.

sections.heading: Three action particles
sections.body: パンをたべます means eat bread. がっこうにいきます means go to school. うちでべんきょうします means study at home.

example.japanese: うちで べんきょうします。

sections.heading: Ask what changes
sections.body: Change the object, destination, or place while keeping the verb frame.

questions.prompt: Which particle marks the object in パンをたべます?
Complete: がっこう ___ いきます。
Which marks the place of studying?
Which sentence means I drink tea?

modules.title: Basic verb, adjective, and question patterns
modules.summary: Make simple present, negative, past, and question sentences.

content.intro: Beginner Japanese becomes flexible when you can state what happens, what does not, and what happened before.

sections.heading: Useful polite forms
sections.body: たべます is eat, たべません is do not eat, and たべました is ate. たべますか asks do you eat?

example.japanese: きのう えいがを みました。

sections.heading: Adjectives and questions
sections.body: おもしろいです means interesting. Use か at the end of a polite question.

questions.prompt: Which means I do not eat?
Which ending makes a polite question?
What does おもしろいです mean?
